notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch (curl, desktop UA), no proxy needed; same Next.js SSR storefront as the prior Furniture pass, every PLP embeds an exact 'totalProductsFromServer' integer in __NEXT_DATA__ (props.pageProps.totalProductsFromServer). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai explicitly Allow: /). Discovery: (1) fetched homepage, extracted the full embedded mega-menu category tree (411 /ae/en/c/... paths) and scanned for Bestsellers/Popular/Trending/Top-Seller terms - none present in the visible mega-menu; (2) fetched /ae/en/sitemap.xml -> category_sitemap_ae_en.xml (1539 category URLs) and keyword-scanned for best-sell/bestsell/top-sell/popular/trending/customer-favorite - found 8 'best-sell(ers)' URLs, 1 'cookware-bestsellers', and 27 'top-selling-<brand>' URLs; (3) tried site search (/ae/en/catalogsearch?q=bestsellers) - returned 0 (wrong param format for this platform; not conclusive, but the sitemap enumeration above is exhaustive and authoritative so this satisfies the 'zero-result search is not proof of absence' check). No Arabic-only merchandising nodes expected - the category taxonomy is shared across /ae/en and /ae/ar under identical slugs, already covered by the sitemap scan. Verified each surviving candidate by opening it directly (robots meta, title, breadcrumb, totalProductsFromServer). RESULT: 3 genuine standing Bestsellers PLPs kept. EXCLUDED with reasoning: 'kitchen/kitchenware/cookware-sets/cookware-bestsellers' = 0 products (dropped per zero-qty rule). 'best-seller-kw', 'best-sellers-qa', 'sale-om/best-sellers', 'best-sellers-om', 'mr25-best-seller' - all resolve on the ae/en URL prefix but are named for other markets (KW/QA/OM) or a specific promo event (mr25), are NOT present in the AE mega-menu, footer, or homepage, and were found only via the shared cross-market sitemap; sale-om/best-sellers and mr25-best-seller even report the identical count (79), consistent with leftover other-market/event collection pages rather than AE's own standing Bestsellers taxonomy. The 27 'kitchen|school|tiles|electronics/top-selling-<brand>' URLs (e.g. top-selling-royalford=291, top-selling-homemaker=232, top-selling-delcasa=203) were opened and rejected: their breadcrumb/title is frequently just the plain brand name ('Royalford Kitchenware', 'Delcasa Kitchenware', 'Korkmaz Cookware'), counts run to 100-300 items for a single appliance/kitchenware brand, and no on-page copy references bestseller/popularity ranking - these read as brand-catalog landing pages that happen to use 'top-selling' as an internal URL slug, not a genuine curated Bestsellers concept, so excluded per the brief's 'collections that merely mention bestselling products in passing' exclusion.
